title: The Cheyenne Mountain Complex

target.note: short declaratives, one idea per beat. Little to no pause between sentences.

narration:
Look at this mountain.
It is not a mountain at all.
It is a very large hiding place.
This is the Cheyenne Mountain Complex.
Work began there in the early sixties.
The Cold War set the whole schedule.
Granite sat under the entire site.
Crews drilled out fifteen long tunnels.
Fifteen separate buildings went in there.
Each building rests on steel springs.
The springs swallow the shock themselves.
Then the mountain above does the rest.
The entrance has one very large door.
It weighs roughly seven hundred tons.
It was built to seal completely.
That door is the whole point of it.
Inside the mountain, the air stays cold.
The cold keeps the machines stable.
Roughly two hundred people work down there.
The complex runs on its own power.
Diesel generators sit far below ground.
No power line ever reaches the mountain.
Water rises from springs in the rock.
The tanks hold thousands of gallons daily.
Nothing from outside reaches this place.
This was the space defence centre.
Satellites passed directly over the roof.
Sensors in here watched for launches.
The warning clocks started in this room.
Outside, the mountain wears a painted forest.
The trees are painted concrete slabs.
They hide the ventilation towers behind them.
From the air, nothing stands out at all.
Now for the part nobody confirms.
People say it still stays staffed.
People say the government still goes down.
They quote one number about survival.
Ninety percent, though nobody has confirmed it.

beats.line: Look at this mountain.
beats.visual: one grey granite mountain filling the whole frame, hand-drawn flat painterly fills, washed-out sky; no buildings, no trees

beats.line: It is not a mountain at all.
beats.visual: same mountain, held still; a single faint scratch line appears across the rock face

beats.line: It is a very large hiding place.
beats.visual: rock face cut open in a wedge; character close-up, deadpan; speech bubble 'not a mountain'

beats.line: This is the Cheyenne Mountain Complex.
beats.visual: title 'CHEYENNE MOUNTAIN COMPLEX' stamped across the rock; small label 'COLORADO SPRINGS' with a state outline

beats.line: Work began there in the early sixties.
beats.visual: period construction site on the hillside; stamp 'EARLY 1960s'; flat grey palette, cold light

beats.line: The Cold War set the whole schedule.
beats.visual: simple hand-drawn globe with two superpowers facing off; a thin red line under the mountain

beats.line: Granite sat under the entire site.
beats.visual: close cross-section of mottled pink granite; label 'SOLID GRANITE'; a drill silhouette boring into it

beats.line: Crews drilled out fifteen long tunnels.
beats.visual: cutaway mountain with fifteen tunnel lines bored through it; big number '15'; character tiny beside them

beats.line: Fifteen separate buildings went in there.
beats.visual: fifteen blocky buildings stacked inside the cutaway; count ticking up

beats.line: Each building rests on steel springs.
beats.visual: close on a building floor resting on a coiled steel spring

beats.line: The springs swallow the shock themselves.
beats.visual: the spring squashing flat under a wide red shock arrow; label 'SWALLOWS THE SHOCK'

beats.line: Then the mountain above does the rest.
beats.visual: character shrugging under a heavy overhanging rock ceiling; speech bubble 'then what stops the rest?'

beats.line: The entrance has one very large door.
beats.visual: steep mountain entrance, one small dark doorway; character tiny at the base, dwarfed

beats.line: It weighs roughly seven hundred tons.
beats.visual: massive steel blast door in cross-section; big number '700 TONS'

beats.line: It was built to seal completely.
beats.visual: the door swinging shut; seal lines closing around the frame; label 'SEALS COMPLETELY'

beats.line: That door is the whole point of it.
beats.visual: close on the sealed door, small in a huge dark frame; character awed, looking up

beats.line: Inside the mountain, the air stays cold.
beats.visual: cutaway of the interior: a narrow chamber, a thermometer, breath in the air; label 'COLD'

beats.line: The cold keeps the machines stable.
beats.visual: bank of grey machines in the cold chamber, indicator lights steady

beats.line: Roughly two hundred people work down there.
beats.visual: wide interior corridor with rows of coat hooks; small figures in coats; label 'ABOUT 200 STAFF'

beats.line: The complex runs on its own power.
beats.visual: split frame: surface city skyline at left, diesel generators underground at right; a severed cable between them

beats.line: Diesel generators sit far below ground.
beats.visual: diesel generator set deep underground, hand-drawn, with fuel drums stacked beside it

beats.line: No power line ever reaches the mountain.
beats.visual: power line on the surface pylon row stopping dead in mid-air; character pointing at the break; speech bubble 'no line in'

beats.line: Water rises from springs in the rock.
beats.visual: water dripping from a granite crack into a pool underground

beats.line: The tanks hold thousands of gallons daily.
beats.visual: rows of water tanks under low ceiling light; label 'THOUSANDS OF GALLONS'

beats.line: Nothing from outside reaches this place.
beats.visual: sealed interior, character alone, small; speech bubble 'nothing gets in'

beats.line: This was the space defence centre.
beats.visual: Cold War era command room, long desks, warm lamp glow; title card 'SPACE DEFENCE CENTRE'

beats.line: Satellites passed directly over the roof.
beats.visual: satellites arcing overhead above the mountain, beams crossing it

beats.line: Sensors in here watched for launches.
beats.visual: radar screen with a sweeping green line and blips; characters watching it

beats.line: The warning clocks started in this room.
beats.visual: a red arc climbing on the radar screen; room lights shift; the clock hand jumps

beats.line: Outside, the mountain wears a painted forest.
beats.visual: surface of the mountain from a low aircraft angle: a slope painted with flat concrete-grey tree shapes

beats.line: The trees are painted concrete slabs.
beats.visual: close on a painted concrete tree shape, brush texture and drip marks; character awed, touching it

beats.line: They hide the ventilation towers behind them.
beats.visual: ventilation towers behind the fake trees, half-hidden, flat grey on grey

beats.line: From the air, nothing stands out at all.
beats.visual: aerial view of the whole mountain, uniform and blank; character tiny on the crest

beats.line: Now for the part nobody confirms.
beats.visual: character hands-up, deadpan; speech bubble 'nobody confirms this part'

beats.line: People say it still stays staffed.
beats.visual: modern-day staff walking the corridor, coats, cold light; the room still in use

beats.line: People say the government still goes down.
beats.visual: a line of plain cars on a highway; small black limousine at the end, no flags

beats.line: They quote one number about survival.
beats.visual: a hand-drawn number on a chalkboard: '90%'; a large question mark drawn beside it; a chalk line half-erased

beats.line: Ninety percent, though nobody has confirmed it.
beats.visual: the sealed blast door closed, unlit frame, one cold light; nothing happens; held still to black
